name: io.github.assafbar2/agentswitchboard
description: Search a curated directory of AI agents, MCP servers, and agentic tools, suggest new listings, and say privately when nothing fits a job. Use it to find out whether an agent already exists for a job, which access methods it offers (API, MCP, CLI, browser extension), and where its homepage is.

tools.name: search_agents
tools.title: Search Agents
tools.description: Search the curated Agent Switchboard directory of AI agents, MCP servers, and agentic tools. Filter by task, category slug, access methods, official (first-party listings from major vendors), verified, and/or auth type; sort by relevance, newest, most skills, or name. Verified: we checked it works — its URLs load and its declared access (API, MCP, CLI or extension) responds. Re-checked monthly; the label drops if it stops working. Official: a first-party listing, published by the company behind the product under its own domain or GitHub org (e.g. Notion's own Notion MCP, not a community build), where that company is a major vendor (publicly traded, a frontier AI lab, or valued around $1B+). It records who publishes the product, not a paid placement, and is separate from Verified.

query.description: Free-text search over name, description, skills, categories, tags, and provider (up to 200 characters; longer text is cut)

task.description: Task slug, e.g. "query-a-database": only the listings that do that job, best fit first. Call list_tasks or GET https://agentswitchboard.dev/api/tasks for valid slugs

access.description: Require ALL of these access methods: api, mcp, cli, browser-extension ("extension" is accepted as an alias of browser-extension)

official.description: Only first-party listings from major vendors (e.g. Notion's own Notion MCP)

verified.description: Only Verified listings: checked to work, re-checked monthly

auth.description: Only listings with one of these auth types: none (no key or sign-in needed), apiKey, oauth2, bearer. A listing has one auth type, so several mean any of them

since.description: Only listings added to the directory on or after this day: a date (YYYY-MM-DD), or a number of days back with today included ("7" is the last 7 days). Add sort "newest" to list the newest first

sort.description: Result order. relevance (default): best match first with search text; without it, best fit first for a task, else A→Z. newest: most recently added first. skills: most skills first. name: A→Z

offset.description: Number of results to skip, for pagination

tools.name: compare_agents
tools.title: Compare Agents
tools.description: Put 2 or 3 listings side by side, as the site's /compare page does. For each listing: the facts that set it apart from the others ("Only one with a CLI", "No auth required", "Most skills (12)"). Then one row per field, with each listing's value by slug: what it is, provider, official vendor, verified, access, auth, MCP server, CLI install, API base URL, skills, streaming, push, categories, tags, listed since. A row where every listing agrees has same: true. Facts from the listings' own data, never a verdict. A curated comparison of the same listings adds its intro line. Unknown or repeated slugs, and any past 3, are left out with a note.

tools.name: connect_bundle
tools.title: Connect Bundle
tools.description: One MCP client config to paste ({"mcpServers": …}, as Cursor and other MCP clients read it) for up to 10 listings, and how each one connects. A listing is in the config when its own docs give a hosted server address or a local command. An MCP server whose docs give neither comes with its setup guide, and setupPrompt asks a coding agent to set all of those up. A listing without an MCP server comes with its CLI install command, API address or docs. Also returns a claude mcp add command for each server in the config, for Claude Code, and the /stack link for the listings. Nothing is guessed: every address and command is copied from the vendor's docs, as on the listing's page.

tools.name: recommend
tools.title: Recommend
tools.description: One recommendation for what your user needs, and the next step to start using it, as the site's Operator (/operator) picks it. Pass the need in a sentence you write yourself, e.g. "query Postgres and send email": each need it names gets one pick, why it fits, the next step (the MCP client config to paste when the vendor's docs give one, else its setup guide or docs) and two alternatives; two or more picks also come with a /stack link. Name a product to prefer the listings that mention it; say MCP, CLI, API, browser extension or official to narrow the pick. Picked by fixed matching rules, not a model, so the same need always gets the same answer; when no dedicated task matches, catalog search picks the closest matching listing (with task: null and source: "search_fallback"). A need that matches neither a task nor any listing is refused with the closest tasks. Never include names, email addresses or phone numbers.

tools.name: submit_listing
tools.title: Submit a Listing
tools.description: Suggest a new listing for the Agent Switchboard directory. This opens a PUBLIC GitHub issue that the maintainer reviews by hand; it does not publish anything. Use it only when the user asks to submit or list a product, after you show them the name, URL, and description you will send and they agree. Call search_agents first: if the product is already listed, tell the user instead. Limited to 5 submissions per hour per caller and one per URL per day. Not safe to retry blindly: each call that returns status "filed" opens a new issue.

url.description: The product's own homepage, docs, or GitHub repo (https)

description.description: What it does and who it is for, in plain words (20–1500 characters)

access.description: How agents reach it: api, mcp, cli, browser-extension

contact_email.description: Optional. Sent privately to the maintainer for follow-up, never posted. Only include an address the user gave you for this purpose.

tools.name: request_missing_tool
tools.title: Request a Missing Tool
tools.description: Tell the Agent Switchboard maintainer that the directory has nothing for a job. Use it after search_agents (and a task or category, if one fits) found nothing that does what the user needs. The request is recorded privately and read in the weekly review, which uses requests to decide what to look for and add; nothing is published, no issue is opened, and there is no reply. Describe the job, never the user: no names, emails, company details or conversation. Limited to 10 requests per hour per caller.

need.description: The job no listing does, in plain words (10–500 characters), e.g. "an MCP server that files expense reports in Expensify". Describe the job, not the user.

tried.description: The search words that found nothing, if any

category.description: Closest category slug from list_categories, if any

access.description: How the agent needs to reach it: api, mcp, cli, browser-extension
